title: Slotcar exemplar rotation journal
content:
Purpose:

Brief scratchpad for the 'slotcar' approach: rotating exemplar sets inside few-shot prompts over time to probe distributional drift and brittle exemplar interactions. Notes are deliberately messy — this is my working notebook for experiments with exemplar rotation scheduling, heuristics for exemplar selection, and quick failure-mode capture.

Why 'slotcar'?
- Imagery: a small set of exemplars are mounted on a rotating carriage (slotcar) that cycles through positions in the prompt template.
- Hypothesis: the positional and temporal ordering of exemplars contributes to emergent biases and fragile generalization. Rotating them can surface sensitivity and create more robust ensembles.

High-level goals:
- Create a minimal harness to rotate exemplar slots deterministically and stochastically.
- Measure metric variance (accuracy/ROUGE/intent F1 / hallucination rate) across rotations.
- Catalog failure modes tied to exemplar position, similarity, and surface overlap.
- Produce a small prompt-library pattern (templates + meta-tags) that can be reused across teams.

Protocol (current):
1) Build canonical prompt template with N slots (N=3 for initial experiments).
2) Keep the same few-shot set, but rotate examples across slots: deterministic rotation (1->2,2->3,3->1) and random shuffle.
3) Track outputs for 200 random seeds per rotation style. Capture: top-1 answer, confidence proxy (logprob sum), token length, hallucination flag (manual + automatic heuristics).
4) Run with two models: open-model-v1-16k and open-model-v0-8k-quant (as a secondary).

Template (base):
-- TEMPLATE A (instruction-first) --
You are a helpful assistant.
Example 1:
Input: {EX1_IN}
Output: {EX1_OUT}

Example 2:
Input: {EX2_IN}
Output: {EX2_OUT}

Example 3:
Input: {EX3_IN}
Output: {EX3_OUT}

Now respond to the user query below.
User: {QUERY}
Assistant:

Notes: the bracket tokens denote slots that will be filled by each exemplar. We'll produce small wrappers to inject slot ids so we can rotate.

Prompt variants I'm testing (short list):
- Instr-first (above)
- Instr-last: put instruction after examples
- Example-format: change 'Input/Output' -> 'Q/A' -> 'Case: /Result:' (surface variant)
- Topic-anchoring: append a one-line anchor describing the domain after each exemplar. (helps troubleshoot topical leakage)

Few-shot sets (examples) — intentionally simple, from internal microtask dataset: (these are paraphrased)
Set S1 (intent-mapping, 3 exemplars):
EX1_IN: "How do I change my payment method?"
EX1_OUT: "Go to Settings > Billing > Payment Methods and add or update card."
EX2_IN: "Can I export my data?"
EX2_OUT: "Yes — Settings > Export, choose timeframe, click Start Export."
EX3_IN: "Is there mobile app?"
EX3_OUT: "Yes, iOS and Android. Search 'Redwood Inference' in the app store."

Set S2 (rewriting/clarity):
EX1_IN: "Shorten: We are pleased to inform you about the release of a new API version that includes multiple improvements."
EX1_OUT: "Release: new API version with performance improvements."
EX2_IN: "Rewrite for slack: The deployment will be paused for up to 30 minutes."
EX2_OUT: "Heads-up: deploying now; may take ~30 minutes."
EX3_IN: "Summarize: On Friday, we saw a 5% drop in tail throughput across regions."
EX3_OUT: "Friday: 5% drop in tail throughput across regions."

Rotation modes:
- deterministic-rotate: shift once per inference batch (position i -> i+1 mod N).
- epoch-rotate: rotate after fixed number of examples (useful for systematic bias detection).
- random-shuffle: fully shuffle exemplar order each call (measure high-variance baseline).

Initial observations (quick notes):
- For S1 (intent mapping), rotation changed the exact phrasing of the selected canned output ~12% of the time (synonym swaps) but intent detection remained stable.
- For S2 (rewrites), rotation produced a higher rate of truncation/hallucinated specifics when the exemplar with the shortest target was in slot 1. (Potential position-length anchoring)
- Models with narrower context windows (v0-8k-quant) showed larger sensitivity to exemplar ordering than v1-16k.

Failure modes seen so far:
- 'Anchor bleed': exemplar with explicit verbatim phrase leaches into model response even when irrelevant (e.g., 'Settings > Billing' appears when query about profile settings).
- 'False exemplar inversion': model copies EX2_OUT but swaps entities from EX1_IN (mixup). Often happens when exemplars share overlapping named entities.
- 'Positional overconfidence': slot 1 frequently biases the model to prefer the structure/length of its output (short→short responses).
- 'Chain hallucinations': when rotating, occasionally the model stitches fragments from two exemplars producing a plausible but incorrect instruction (dangerous for user-facing docs).

Quick metric heuristics (what I'm logging):
- exact_match: boolean vs gold (when available)
- answer_length_delta: tokens(response)-tokens(mean exemplar outputs)
- hallucination_flag: auto heuristics (copied url pattern? conflicting entity?) + manual spot checks
- slot_entropy: diversity of top tokens per slot across seeds

Small debug prompts I use to reproduce common cases:
Reproduce anchor bleed:
Prompt: template A filled with S1 but set EX1_OUT to include a very specific path 'Settings > Billing > Payment Methods'. Query: 'How do I change my username?'
Expected: mention profile or account settings. Observed: 'Go to Settings > Billing > Payment Methods...' (wrong area).

Reproduce false exemplar inversion:
- Set exemplars with shared entity 'AcmeCorp' and 'Acme Support' in different pairs; query about unsubscribing -> model outputs a mixed instruction with 'contact Acme Support at support@example.com' + 'visit Billing > subscriptions'.

Notes to self (TODOs):
- Automate rotation harness in probe-experiments repo; add a job that runs 1k rotations overnight and writes CSV to S3. (PR in progress: linked_artifacts above)
- Add automated entity overlap detection when constructing few-shot sets to warn/avoid shared tokens across exemplars.
- Try slot-weighted prompting (prefix each slot with a small instruction emphasizing not to copy entities). See if that reduces entanglement.
- Test with cached-prefix setup (simulate Redwood prefix caching) to ensure caching doesn't amplify positional biases.

Experimental logs (condensed) — sample entries:
2024-10-12 | model: open-v1-16k | set: S1 | mode: deterministic-rotate | runs: 300 | intent-stability: 96% | phrasing-var: 12% | notable: anchor-bleed 8 cases
2024-11-02 | model: open-v0-8k-quant | set: S2 | mode: random-shuffle | runs: 500 | exact_match: 72% | hallucination_flag: 14% | notable: truncation when short exemplar in slot1
2025-01-15 | model: open-v1-16k | set: mixed-domain | mode: epoch-rotate | runs: 1000 | slot_entropy increase vs baseline: +0.18 | notable: chain hallucination 4 instances (escalate to Marcus)

Practical heuristics I'm leaning toward:
- Avoid high-entity-overlap exemplars in the same few-shot set.
- For rewrite/conciseness tasks prefer exemplars with consistent target length to avoid positional length bias.
- If rotation causes variance but preserves truthfulness, consider rotation-ensemble (sample top-k from different rotations, then canonicalize by heuristic scoring).

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- Does prefix-level anchoring (e.g., add 'Do not copy named entities from examples' before the query) reduce false exemplar inversion without hurting quality?
- Is there a lower bound on exemplar similarity where rotation becomes irrelevant (i.e., if exemplars are fully orthogonal)?
- Can we synthesize adversarial exemplars to probe worst-case slot interactions and then use adversarial training to harden prompt templates?

Rough sketch of a reproducible experiment for the team (copyable):
- dataset: internal-microtask-intents (n=1500 heldout)
- exemplar selection: 3 nearest neighbors by embedding to query (control: random 3)
- rotation modes: no-rotation (fixed order), deterministic-rotate, random-shuffle
- metrics: intent-accuracy, phrasing-consistency, hallucination_flag
- run: 3 seeds, 500 queries each, two models: v1-16k, v0-8k-quant
- output: CSV columns: query_id, rotation_mode, slot_order, model, response, exact_match, hallucination_flag, logprob_sum

Slack notes:
- discussed initial anchor-bleed with #applied-ml on 2024-10-16 (thread: quick link pinned in PR). Marcus to try slot-weighting hack.

Final (for now)
- This is my working scratchpad. Keep it rough. I will extract the reproducible experiment into an Issues checklist and a small runner script in the repo.
- If you want to play: run deterministic-rotate on S2 with v0-8k-quant and look for truncation cases — they're fast to find.

— Ava
